Neither option in the team note is correct: lactate is made from pyruvate, so it cannot rise when pyruvate formation stops, and it rises when oxygen is scarce, not readily available. Lactate production increases when glycolysis produces pyruvate faster than the mitochondria can oxidize it, as in high-intensity exercise with limited oxygen delivery, a high cytosolic NADH/NAD⁺ ratio, or adrenergic stimulation. I'd recommend correcting the team note before it propagates.

CONFIDENCE: 85
